messages.subject: Display missing countries from data?
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm a graduate student working on a political science paper on state recognition. I'm trying to map (thanks to rworldmap!) the recognition of Kosovo as only half the world recognizes Kosovo as a country.

My issue is that I would like to see which countries R says are not included in my data. The R output states, "54 codes from the map weren't represented in your data." . I did use the verbose='TRUE' command to see which of my countries could not match rworldmap's list/code (only one), but now I would like to know which countries I'm missing.

Any help would be appreciated...

Cheers,
Holly Gerrity
hg...@georgetown.edu
gerr...@cougars.csusm.edu

messages.subject_clean: [rworldmap group] Display missing countries from data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Holly,

Thanks, interesting sounding project and good question.

I used to get rworldmap to output the list of non matched 'countries' (some are dependencies etc.) but I got fed up with long lists being output all the time because datasets seldom have all 'countries' that are in the full map.

Try the code (replacing dF and joinCode with what you are using), and let us know how you get on.

Best,
Andy

###### bits to change ###################
joinCode <- "ISO3"
#creating a test dataset
dF <- data.frame(ISO3=c("AFG","AGO","ALB","GBR"),test=c(1,2,3,4))
#########################################

#get the map from rworldmap - can change to higher resolution
sPDF <- getMap(resolution="coarse")

matchPosnsInUserData <- match(as.character(sPDF[[joinCode]]), as.character(dF[[joinCode]]))

#these are the codes in lookup that aren't found in user data
codesMissingFromUserData <- as.character( sPDF[[joinCode]][is.na <http://is.na>(matchPosnsInUserData)] )
namesMissingFromUserData <- as.character( sPDF[["NAME"]][is.na <http://is.na>(matchPosnsInUserData)] )

#to view
namesMissingFromUserData

#or get the whole dataframe
dFmissingFromUserData <- sPDF@data[is.na <http://is.na>(matchPosnsInUserData),]

#then you can subset by TYPE
dFmissingCountries <- dFmissingFromUserData[ which(dFmissingFromUserData$TYPE=="Sovereign country" | dFmissingFromUserData$TYPE=="Country"), ]

#to view
fix(dFmissingCountries)

messages.subject: Somaliland and Somalia
messages.body_plain: rworldmap distinguishes between Somalia and Somaliland, which is a bit unconventional. Somaliland is generally considered part of Somalia and has no ISO3 country code of its own. It was by pure guessing that I figured out that rworldmap uses SOL (which is "unofficially" used for Solomon Islands, according to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_codes:_S.

messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] push to cran
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeroen,

Thanks and apologies, I had intended a CRAN release before now, however before that I want to make sure I haven't broken anything which requires a little time.

No-one pays me to to develop rworldmap and I've recently gone freelance so getting some cash in the door has been a time priority.

For other readers your original question was about French Guiana which doesn't appear in the CRAN version, but does in the development version obtainable by :

install.packages("rworldmap", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")

(inote that I plan to change where the development version is hosted soon).

Whether this was a bug or not is open to debate. French Guiana is an overseas region of France & so some users might want to include it as France - one of those tricky 'what is a country?' things ;-).

Best wishes,
Andy

messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] Somaliland and Somalia
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeroen,

rworldmap uses the wonderful Natural Earth data for country boundaries (http://www.naturalearthdata.com) the ISO code for Somaliland comes from there.

To find out the code used for a known country name you could have done something like this :
dFmapData <- getMap()@data
dFmapData$ISO3[ which(dFmapData$ADMIN=="Somaliland") ]

For those interested in more detail rworldmap uses version 1.3 of the Natural Earth data and does various tweaks and checks to get the data into R. This includes adding countries that are missing from the lower resolution data from the higher resolution data (although they might not be visible you might want to put a bubble there).
The code is here :
https://r-forge.r-project.org/scm/viewvc.php/rworldmapSetup/saveMapPolygons.r?view=markup&root=rworldmap

Best,
Andy
